citation: Jindal & Liu, Opinion Spam and Analysis
task: Opinion spam taxonomy and detection (Type 1 untruthful, Type 2 brand-only, Type 3 non-reviews)
data: Amazon.com crawl (June 2006): ~5.8M reviews, 2.14M reviewers, ~6.7M products; detailed analysis on mProducts (228,422 reviews); 470 manually labeled Type 2/3 spam reviews
method: Duplicate detection (2-gram Jaccard >= 90%); logistic regression with 36 review/reviewer/product features; duplicates used as positives for Type 1
results: Types 2+3: AUC 98.7% (all features), 90% text-only; Type 1 (duplicate-trained): AUC 78%; helpfulness feedback does not separate spam
limitations: Authors call it an initial investigation; duplicates are only a proxy for Type 1 spam; Type 1 could not be labeled manually; single site and category, 2006 data
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: origin of the 3 spam types; ViSpamReviews' SPAM-1/2/3 labels follow this scheme; basis for Taxonomy

citation: Ott, Choi, Cardie & Hancock, Finding Deceptive Opinion Spam by Any Stretch of the Imagination
data: Gold-standard set of 800 positive hotel reviews: 400 truthful (TripAdvisor, 20 Chicago hotels, 5-star) and 400 deceptive (Amazon Mechanical Turk, 20 per hotel)
method: Three approaches: POS genre features, LIWC psycholinguistic features, n-gram text categorization; linear SVM and Naive Bayes
results: LIWC+bigrams SVM 89.8% accuracy (bigrams alone 89.6%); POS 73.0%; LIWC 76.8%; 3 human judges 53.1%-61.9% (kappa 0.11)
limitations: Crowdsourced fakes may differ from real-world fakes; positive hotel reviews only; some low-effort MTurk submissions (~12% under 1 minute); small human-judge sample
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: shows text alone detects deceptive reviews and humans do poorly; classic content-branch baseline (n-gram SVM)
verification: Verified against arXiv PDF 1107.4557 and ACL Anthology

citation: Mukherjee, Liu & Glance, Spotting Fake Reviewer Groups in Consumer Reviews
task: Group spam / fake reviewer group detection
data: Amazon reviews (crawled 2006, updated 2010), manufactured products: 53,469 reviewers, 109,518 reviews, 39,392 products; 7,052 candidate groups, 2,431 labeled by 8 judges (Fleiss kappa 0.79)
method: Frequent itemset mining for candidate groups (min support 3, >= 2 reviewers); 8 group behavior indicators (time window, rating deviation, content similarity, size, support...); GSRank relation-based ranking
results: GSRank AUC 0.93 / 0.95 (spamicity thresholds 0.5 / 0.7) vs RankBoost 0.86 / 0.88 and best SVM 0.81-0.86
limitations: Dated Amazon data; subjective expert labels, only candidate groups labeled; cannot tell sockpuppets from several people; no IP data; misses groups that acted only once
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: core reference for the pattern branch (group spam indicators); inspires burst and similarity features

citation: Rayana & Akoglu, Collective Opinion Spam Detection: Bridging Review Networks and Metadata (SpEagle)
task: Joint detection of fake reviews, spammers and target products
data: Yelp filtered/recommended reviews: YelpChi (Chicago hotels and restaurants), YelpNYC, YelpZip
method: Markov Random Field on user-review-product graph, loopy belief propagation; priors from text and behavioral features (rating deviation, burstiness, content similarity...); variants SpEagle+, SpLite
results: Review-ranking AP on YelpChi 0.3236 (SpEagle) vs 0.1518 and 0.1067 for baselines; 1% labels raise user AP from 0.3393 to 0.3967; SpLite+ comparable and much faster
limitations: Ground truth is Yelp's filter, not verified fraud; approximate inference; modest absolute precision; hand-designed features; only Yelp restaurants/hotels
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: shows combining text, metadata and network helps; supports the fusion idea
verification: Verified against paper PDF; venue (KDD 2015) from search result titles

citation: Salminen, Kandpal, Kamel, Jung & Jansen, Creating and detecting fake reviews of online products
venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services, vol. 64, art. 102771 (DOI 10.1016/j.jretconser.2021.102771)
task: Machine-generated fake reviews and their detection

citation: Van Dinh, Luu & Nguyen, Detecting Spam Reviews on Vietnamese E-commerce Websites (ViSpamReviews)
task: Vietnamese spam review detection (binary and 3 spam types)
data: ViSpamReviews: ~19,868 collected, ~19,000 annotated; split 14,306 / 1,590 / 3,974; labels NO-SPAM, SPAM-1 fake, SPAM-2 brand-only, SPAM-3 non-review; Cohen kappa 0.72 (Task 1) and 0.68 (Task 2) after guideline revision (0.43/0.44 before)
results: PhoBERT best: macro F1 86.89 (binary) and 72.17 (spam type); Text-CNN 77.89/64.74; LSTM 77.24/66.58; BERT4News 86.16/62.62
limitations: Platforms not named in the paper; text-only (no reviewer or time information); spam-type task is hard (macro F1 ~72)
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: Very high: Vietnamese benchmark and baseline; annotation process (kappa 0.43 -> 0.72 after revision) is a model for our guideline v1
verification: Verified against arXiv/ar5iv; dataset reported on GitHub sonlam1102/vispamdetection (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the paper); check dataset licence before use

citation: Van Dinh & Luu, Metadata Integration for Spam Reviews Detection on Vietnamese E-commerce Websites
venue: International Journal of Asian Language Processing (arXiv 2405.13292)
task: Vietnamese spam review detection with metadata
method: PhoBERT + product category + SPhoBERT (PhoBERT+SentenceBERT) product description features
results: Spam classification macro F1 87.22% (+1.64%); spam type accuracy 73.49% (+1.93%) over baseline
limitations: Gains are small; only product metadata, no reviewer behavior
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: evidence that metadata helps Vietnamese spam detection; supports fusion

citation: Reimers & Gurevych, Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
task: Sentence embeddings for similarity search and clustering

citation: Kleinberg, Bursty and Hierarchical Structure in Streams
data: E-mail (~34,000 messages), SIGMOD/VLDB and STOC/FOCS titles, State of the Union addresses
method: Infinite-state automaton; higher states emit items at faster rates; dynamic programming finds the cheapest state sequence; hierarchical bursts
results: Qualitative: detects meaningful bursts in the data sets above
limitations: Parameter sensitive (s, gamma); qualitative evaluation only; exponential-gap model assumption; single-user e-mail corpus
relevance_to_ReviewGuard: High: burst score for sudden waves of reviews on a product or shop
